title: Past modals
instructions: Complete each sentence with a past modal and the verb in brackets.

items.q: The streets are wet. It ______ (rain) last night.
She ______ (see) me - she walked straight past without saying hello.
I'm not sure where my keys are. I ______ (leave) them at the office.
You ______ (tell) me it was a formal dinner! I was the only one in jeans.
We ______ (buy) so much food - half of it went to waste.
He looks exhausted. He ______ (work) all night.
That ______ (be) Tom you saw at the party - he's in Canada this month.
Why did you walk home alone at 3 a.m.? You ______ (get) attacked!
I ______ (take) a taxi because Anna offered me a lift, so I saved some money.
They ______ (forget) about the meeting - they're never late.

title: Reporting passives and the causative
instructions: Complete the second sentence so it means the same as the first. Write only the missing words.

items.q:
People believe that the painting is a fake.
The painting ______ a fake.

People say that he earned millions in the 1990s.
He ______ millions in the 1990s.

Reports suggest that the company is planning layoffs.
The company ______ planning layoffs.

They think the thieves escaped through the window.
The thieves ______ through the window.

A mechanic is repairing my car at the moment.
I'm ______ at the moment.

I persuaded my brother to help me move.
I got ______ me move.

It is expected that prices will rise.
Prices ______ rise.

Someone stole her bag on the train.
She ______ on the train.

The windows need cleaning.
The windows need ______.

It was alleged that the minister had lied.
The minister ______ lied.

title: Participle clauses
instructions: Complete the second sentence using a participle clause. Write only the missing words.

items.q:
Because I didn't know anyone, I left early.
______ anyone, I left early.

After she had finished the report, she went home.
______ the report, she went home.

The castle, which was built in the 12th century, attracts thousands of visitors.
______ in the 12th century, the castle attracts thousands of visitors.

Anyone who wishes to attend must register by Friday.
Anyone ______ to attend must register by Friday.

As he had been warned twice, he knew the risks.
______ twice, he knew the risks.

The people who were injured in the accident were taken to hospital.
The people ______ in the accident were taken to hospital.

While I was walking home, I saw an old friend.
______ home, I saw an old friend.

Since I had never been to Asia before, I found the trip overwhelming.
______ to Asia before, I found the trip overwhelming.

title: Emphasis, substitution and ellipsis
instructions: Write ONE word in each gap.

items.q: "Will it rain tomorrow?" "I hope ______." (You want a sunny day.)
"Is the shop closed already?" "I'm afraid ______."
I don't like horror films, and ______ does my sister.
You say I never help, but I ______ help! I did the dishes yesterday.
Some candidates may already have experience. If ______, they will start on a higher salary.
These shoes are too small. Do you have any bigger ______?
I asked him to apologise, but he refused to do ______.
There is no evidence ______ to support this claim.
"Would you like to join us for dinner?" "I'd love ______!"
She is ______ far the best candidate we've interviewed.

title: Subjunctive and fixed expressions
instructions: Put the verb in brackets into the correct form, or complete the fixed expression with ONE word.

items.q: The doctor recommended that he ______ (rest) for two weeks.
It is essential that every employee ______ (be) informed before Monday.
items.why: Formal: 'be'. BrE: 'should be'. The indicative ('is', 'takes') is also normal in British English, just less formal.

items.q: They insisted that she ______ (not / travel) alone.
The committee proposed that the rule ______ (change).
It's vital that he ______ (take) his medication every day.
I suggest that she ______ (apply) for the position.
______ that as it may, we still need a decision by Friday.
We'll finish the project on time, come what ______.
You should of told me earlier.
a: You should have told me earlier.

items.q: He is said to be born in Mexico.
a: He is said to have been born in Mexico.

items.q: I suggested him to take the train.
a: I suggested that he take the train.
I suggested that he should take the train.
I suggested he take the train.

items.q: I cut my hair yesterday at the new salon.
a: I had my hair cut yesterday at the new salon.
I got my hair cut yesterday at the new salon.

items.q: Having finished dinner, the dishes were washed.
a: Having finished dinner, we washed the dishes.
Having finished dinner, I washed the dishes.

items.q: She can't have saw the message.
a: She can't have seen the message.

items.q: It is essential that he arrived on time tomorrow.
a: It is essential that he arrive on time tomorrow.
It is essential that he should arrive on time tomorrow.
It is essential that he arrives on time tomorrow.

items.q: The car needs to repair.
a: The car needs to be repaired.
